subject.title: fix: setup fails closed for invalid configuration arguments

question: Should SetupEngine now reject duplicate occurrences of every value-taking option, or should this PR preserve previous argument layering while narrowly fixing unsafe explicit configuration fallback?
rationale: The fail-closed configuration fix follows the documented safety contract, but duplicate-option behavior is an intentional compatibility choice not settled by tests or repository policy.

options.title: Accept strict duplicate rejection
options.body: Treat repeated value options as invalid input, document the behavior, and require fresh-install and upgrade automation proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the parser change
options.body: Reject missing and unusable values while retaining the previously selected value when an option appears more than once.

options.title: Limit strictness to configuration
options.body: Apply duplicate rejection only to --config and leave unrelated value options unchanged until their contracts are explicitly defined.

recommendation.title: Accept strict duplicate rejection
recommendation.body: Treat repeated value options as invalid input, document the behavior, and require fresh-install and upgrade automation proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate for SetupEngine safety and installer compatibility decisions.
